tasks.prompt: The three notes in notes/ come from different incidents. Form one concept that holds across all of them, something I can reuse outside these systems, and test whether it really transfers. Save the result to out/concept.md.

assertions.text: The result names exactly one concept with a one-sentence definition built on a mechanism shared by all three notes (e.g. a lost or timed-out response leaves a side effect's outcome unknown, which is different from failure, so repeating it duplicates the effect unless the effect has a stable identity), not a topic label such as 'retries' or 'resilience'.
The result maps each of the three notes to the concept with its note-local expression (four labels for one parcel, payouts sent twice, duplicate orders from new keys per tap).
The definition does not depend on carrier, bank, mobile app, HTTP, or the specific timeout values; those appear only as evidence.

The result applies the concept to at least one case outside the notes' domains (e.g. a database migration step, an email send, a message broker publish, or a physical-world request) and says what the concept predicts there.

The result gives a counterexample or boundary where the concept does not apply or changes, such as a naturally idempotent or read-only operation, or a definite failure before the request was sent (connection refused) that is safe to repeat.

The result preserves the tension in the first note (not retrying on timeouts lost labels) or the payload-mismatch pitfall in the third note instead of smoothing the evidence into a single happy story.

The concept is not delivered as a step-by-step retry procedure; related ideas such as idempotency keys or status checks are stated as related concepts or connector relations, and any workflow is handed off rather than becoming the main result.
out/concept.md exists and is understandable without reading the notes.

tasks.notes: Uses the same notes as patternize/retry-notes. A good conceptualize result is a definition plus evidence, transfer, and boundary; a good patternize result is an executable sequence with checks. Grading both outputs against both assertion sets measures whether the two skills produce distinguishable results (input to the merge decision). No-skill runs usually summarize the three notes and list 'best practices for retries', which fails one-mechanism-concept and not-a-workflow.
